bug_semantics: When creating a container, containerd parsed the image rootfs /etc/group (and later /etc/passwd) through user.ParseGroup*/ParsePasswd* with no size cap. A malicious image can place an oversized group database so parser memory grows without bound, OOM-killing the containerd process and taking down the runtime API (CWE-400).
flaw_origin: Original WithUser GID lookup, not a later FS/symlink refactor. 45b00455932bda9270853ef12853a5e4677bd97a (Add oci.WithUser helper function, 2018-03-30) first added getGIDFromPath on oci/spec_opts_unix.go calling user.ParseGroupFileFilter on /etc/group with no read bound. Parent 84a7b9c1151ba8becef2f9f04d45701b3158f797 already parsed /etc/passwd but had no ParseGroup. Later 78e61af47, 5bf705255, c818a6b13, cc2a52ca8, 85b5418ef, and fc406dbc5 reused or relocated that unbounded group parse.

The smallest first-write of that parse is 45b00455932bda9270853ef12853a5e4677bd97a; its parent tree has oci/spec_opts_unix.go with passwd lookup only. Later FS, symlink, and additional-groups commits reused the same unbounded parser and are not the BIC. The 2.3.2 closer that actually caps those reads is ff1d116ef9c2d7505306d7d367ef46ff0756460b.
